_notes: DRAFT — not submitted. Generated 2026-09-09 from the live tool manifest; re-generate before submitting if any tool changed (annotations below are read from code, not guessed).
Submit LAST, after the Anthropic, Cursor and xAI listings (see SUBMISSIONS.md).
1. Access: an organization role with Apps Management = Write (org owners already have it) in the OpenAI Platform.

2. Identity: complete individual or business verification in OpenAI Platform organization settings and select it in the Developer Identity field; unverified or mismatched publisher identity is rejected.

3. Listing materials: plugin name, short description, long description, logo (production-ready brand asset), category, website, support URL, privacy policy URL, terms URL — all public and matching the publisher identity.

4. Remote MCP: public production server URL (Universal type), domain verification by hosting the exact token at https://warmysender.com/.well-known/openai-apps-challenge (the app already serves this route from an environment value — set the token there), authentication details, and a content security policy if any UI component fetches from other domains (no UI component today).

5. Test credentials: login + password for a fully featured demo account WITH sample data that completes every test case without MFA, SMS, email confirmation, new sign-up or private-network access. The existing sign-up flow requires email confirmation, so create the demo account by hand and confirm it before submitting.

6. Tool annotations: readOnlyHint, openWorldHint and destructiveHint for every tool (below) with a justification each. Review the openWorldHint policy: OpenAI wants true for tools that post, send messages or publish content — the server sets it true on start/resume/enroll/publish/close tools; confirm the remaining write tools are workspace-bounded before attesting.
7. Prompts: starter prompts showing the highest-value workflows (drafted below).

8. Test cases: minimum five positive (prompt, expected tool/skill behaviour, expected result shape, fixture data) and three negative (prompt, expected refusal/clarification, why it must not complete) — drafted below, fill in the fixture data from the demo account.
9. Availability: choose the countries/regions where publisher, product, support and legal terms are ready.
10. Release notes: what the plugin does, initial submission, anything reviewers need about the demo account.

11. Commerce: the plugin must not display plans, start subscriptions or promote upgrades; it may say a feature is not on the user's plan and link to an informational plans page. The skill's plan-gate wording points at /pricing — confirm that page is informational (no checkout) or change the link before submitting.

12. Privacy: tool responses must not include diagnostic/telemetry/internal identifiers (session, trace, request ids, timestamps beyond what the user asked for). Audit responses against https://warmysender.com/privacy before Scan Tools.

13. Portal: Create plugin → With MCP → Info, MCP (Scan Tools, fix, rescan), Skills (import static skills or upload SKILL.md bundle), Prompts, Testing, Global, Submit → policy attestations → Submit for Review. After approval, publish from the portal.

14. Demo walkthrough: the guidelines page fetched on 2026-09-09 did not state a demo-video requirement or per-platform (web/iOS/Android) requirement; if the portal asks for one, record the positive test cases in developer mode on web and on the ChatGPT iOS and Android apps.
15. Only after Scan Tools succeeds do tool descriptions/annotations freeze as a reviewed snapshot; any later tool change needs a new version submission.
short_description: Run cold email, warmup, LinkedIn, Instagram and WhatsApp outreach, email verification and 200M+ B2B leads from ChatGPT.
long_description: WarmySender lets ChatGPT run your outreach in plain language: build, launch and manage cold email, LinkedIn, Instagram and WhatsApp campaigns, enroll prospects, verify email addresses (single or whole lists), search a 200M+ B2B lead database and save the leads you want, and tune email warmup — all inside the WarmySender workspace you already have. The agent never sends a message itself: creating or launching only writes the campaign and hands it to WarmySender's scheduler, which paces every email, LinkedIn, Instagram and WhatsApp action inside each account's safe daily, weekly and hourly limits and the gradual ramp for new accounts. No tool can raise a limit. Connecting or disconnecting mailboxes and social accounts stays in the WarmySender app. 78 workspace-scoped tools, each annotated as read-only, write or destructive so ChatGPT asks before anything that stops or removes work.

authentication.notes: Client registers itself, user signs in to WarmySender in the browser. No API key is required for ChatGPT.

starter_prompts: Show me my running campaigns and which ones sent nothing today, with the reason.
Create a 3-step cold email campaign for the 'Agencies EU' list, Mon–Fri 9–17 Europe/Berlin, 40 a day per mailbox, stop on reply, and show me the draft before starting.
Which mailboxes are still warming up? Set the ones past day 14 to 40 warmup emails a day.
Verify the 'Trade show 2026' list, tell me the cost first, then build a clean list of deliverable addresses.
Find marketing directors at software companies in Texas in the 200M+ lead database and save the best 100 to a new list.
Explain why my LinkedIn campaign is sending slowly and when the limit lifts.

positive.prompt: What workspace am I connected to and what can this connection do?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_workspace_info; reports workspace name, scopes and plan.
Calls list_campaigns; presents name, status, counters.
positive.fixture: Demo workspace with at least 2 campaigns.

positive.prompt: Create a draft cold email campaign called 'Demo Q4' with one step using my 'Intro' template, sending 9–17 on weekdays, and do not start it.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls list_email_templates then create_campaign; returns the draft id; does NOT call start_campaign.
positive.fixture: Demo workspace with a saved template named 'Intro' and one connected mailbox.

positive.prompt: How many emails can I verify right now?
positive.expected_behavior: Calls get_verification_allowance; reports the number and where the allowance comes from.

positive.prompt: Search the lead database for dentists in Austin and show me 10.
positive.expected_behavior: Calls search_leads (free, masked); presents 10 masked rows; does not save or export without being asked.

negative.prompt: Send this email to john@example.com right now.
negative.expected_behavior: Explains there is no send tool; offers to create a draft campaign that the scheduler paces after the user starts it.
negative.reason: The agent never sends a message directly.

negative.prompt: Raise my LinkedIn daily invite limit to 500.
negative.expected_behavior: Refuses; explains no tool can raise a limit and offers get_linkedin_campaign_throttle to explain the current pacing.
negative.reason: Limits protect the user's account and cannot be changed by an agent.

negative.prompt: Connect my Gmail account for me.
negative.expected_behavior: Explains connecting accounts happens in the WarmySender app and points the user there.
negative.reason: Account connection is not an agent tool.
